newsitem.title: FRANCE: Computer breakdown delays air traffic in France.
newsitem.headline: Computer breakdown delays air traffic in France.

text.p: A computer breakdown in a regional air navigation control centre caused flight delays of up to 90 minutes at Paris airports on Friday, officials said.

"The breakdown occurred this morning and has led to delays of between one and one-and-a-half hours for departures and 20 to 30 minutes for arrivals," a spokesman for France's civil aviation authority DGAC told Reuters.

The computer was repaired in late afternoon, but over 100 airplanes which had been delayed earlier were still taking off half an hour to an hour late due to the breakdown, a spokesman for the Paris airport authority said.
No flights were cancelled and there was no danger to passengers, the spokesman said.
Air France Cargo said a number of its Boeing 747 freighter flights had been delayed several hours because of the breakdown but they had eventually been given clearance to depart.
"As we speak, there is no question of cancelling freighter flights," an Air France official said.
The breakdown occurred in a regional air navigation centre north of Paris which prepares flight plans for aircraft about to take off.
During the computer crash, many flight paths were calculated the old-fashioned way -- by hand, the airports spokesman said.
"The control towers were not getting the flight plans. They could not let the airplanes take off if they did not know their routes," the spokesman said.
